name: Accessibility Horizon and Reachability Limit Law
purpose: Define bounded reachability and accessibility horizons across the orientation array.

candidate_law_statement.informal: A locus or channel has an accessibility horizon when continuation influence becomes inadmissible, too weak, too lossy, or unreachable under finite transport and reconstruction constraints.

formal.accessibility_horizon_candidate: H_A(α) := { β ∈ {-(i)_α} : Reach(α,β) fails under admissibility, finite-flux, decay, or reconstruction constraints }
formal.reachable_domain_candidate: D_A(α) := { β : β ∈ CSI(α), ||NavT(ω_α,ω_β)|| < ∞, and Π_A remains defined }
formal.decay_condition: Reachability may decay when W_CSI(α,β), reinforcement support, or admissibility margin falls below declared threshold.
formal.reconstruction_limit_clause: Some inaccessible regions may remain observationally compressed or reconstructively ambiguous rather than absolutely absent.
formal.non_spacetime_clause: Accessibility horizons are array-topology limits, not primitive spacetime light cones or physical causal horizons.
